history_findings.finding: The deleted frank_adaptive_vision.py implemented a two-stage perception policy: Stage 1 fast detectors at about 100 ms always, Stage 2 VLM via Ollama at about 800 ms only when an escalation policy judged Stage 1 insufficient.
history_findings.current_mapping: Direct ancestor of the current cheap-gate/familiar-fast-path versus deeper-perception routing architecture.

history_findings.finding: Its EscalationEngine represented an explicit decision object with needs_vlm, reason, confidence_without_vlm and triggers. It clamped a heuristic confidence score and escalated when confidence fell below 0.55.
history_findings.current_mapping: Useful routing-state shape, but the historical heuristic confidence is not a calibrated open-set familiarity probability.

history_findings.finding: The policy contained cheap-path overrides: text-heavy screenshots could skip VLM because OCR was considered sufficient (confidence 0.9), and diagrams with text labels could skip VLM at confidence 0.75.
history_findings.current_mapping: Strong predecessor for modality/task-specific compute avoidance: cheap evidence can terminate the path when it is sufficient, while uncertainty escalates.

history_findings.finding: Commit 0fd27f23 explicitly deleted frank_adaptive_vision.py and frank_visual_pipeline.py and replaced them with FrankEye, while adding a DINOv2 INT8 ONNX local visual path.
history_findings.current_mapping: Project-Frankenstein moved from conditional external-VLM escalation toward a unified local CPU inference module; the routing idea survived conceptually but the named adaptive pipeline disappeared from HEAD.

history_findings.finding: Historical Project-Frankenstein used the word adaptive primarily for adaptive inference/escalation, not for online user-specific classifier learning. No inspected evidence in this deleted file establishes prototype updates, trusted example tiers, sequential class learning, candidate promotion, rollback or user-scoped classifier persistence.
history_findings.current_mapping: Prevents a dangerous lineage error: historical 'adaptive vision' must not be counted as satisfying the current FRANK v0.1 adaptive visual learning requirement.

cross_source_synthesis.pf_deleted_adaptive_vision: adaptive compute routing / escalation based on fast-path sufficiency
cross_source_synthesis.pf_frankeye_head: unified fixed local perception backbone and description pipeline
cross_source_synthesis.current_mvc_contract: user-specific online bounded learning plus calibrated open-set routing, provenance tiers, promotion/rollback/versioning and resource budgets
cross_source_synthesis.synthesis: Current FRANK v0.1 Retina design can legitimately inherit three different historical mechanisms, but they must remain semantically distinct: (1) fast/deep adaptive routing, (2) local reusable perception features, and (3) learned prototype/dictionary memory. The new MVC contract is the first point where all three are required to coexist under explicit provenance/open-set/recovery laws.

negative_results_and_guardrails: Do not equate the historical name 'Adaptive Visual Pipeline' with online adaptive learning.
Do not promote the historical 0.55 escalation threshold or 0.9/0.75 override confidences into current acceptance thresholds; they were heuristic routing constants.
Do not infer that replacing the VLM path with FrankEye preserved every deleted pipeline capability without differential evidence.
Deleted code is historical evidence and must be preserved as lineage even though it is superseded at HEAD.

reuse: Explicit fast-path versus deep-path decision object with reasons/triggers.
Task-sensitive cheap-path termination such as OCR-sufficient screenshots.
Uncertainty-driven escalation instead of always-on expensive perception.
Current FrankEye/DINO-style local features as candidate reusable backbone.
Drive Retina prototype/centroid memory as candidate familiarity layer.
required_modernization: replace heuristic confidence with calibrated known/unknown/conflict semantics where familiarity is used
make user-specific learned state versioned and replayable
add trusted example admission and poisoning resistance
add candidate shadow evaluation, atomic promotion and rollback
measure compute savings and task loss rather than assuming adaptive routing is beneficial

recommended_discriminating_tests: Replay the same screenshot/image set through three policies: always-deep, historical heuristic fast/deep routing, and current MVC familiarity+open-set routing; compare task correctness, escalation rate, latency and CPU/RAM cost.

Separate two ablations: lesion only learned familiarity state while keeping fast/deep policy, then lesion fast/deep policy while keeping classifier predictions. This distinguishes learning benefit from routing benefit.
Include OCR-heavy screenshots, diagrams, recurring UI states, near-neighbor unknowns and genuinely novel scenes to test whether cheap-path exits are appropriately calibrated.
